findings.title: isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process) is never true for spawn processes, so unhealthy flushers are never killed
findings.body: In `_ensure_processes_alive` the kill is now guarded by `isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process)`. Processes here are created with `multiprocessing.get_context("spawn").Process`, which produces `multiprocessing.context.SpawnProcess` instances; `SpawnProcess` is a subclass of `BaseProcess`, not of `multiprocessing.Process` (= `context.Process`). So the isinstance check is False and `process.kill()` is never invoked. A hung (but still alive) flusher process will not be killed before `_create_process_for_shards` starts a replacement, leaking live processes that keep flushing the same shards concurrently — duplicate segment production and growing process count up to MAX_PROCESS_RESTARTS. The same flaw makes `process.terminate()` in `join()` a no-op.

findings.title: join() breaks out of loop leaving remaining processes unterminated
findings.body: In `join`, when the deadline is exceeded the loop `break`s, so any processes after the current index are never waited on nor terminated. On shutdown/rebalance with multiple flusher processes, some child processes are left running (they are daemons, so they die with the parent, but during arroyo rebalances the parent keeps running) and may keep flushing shards that have been reassigned. Also `remaining_time` is computed and unused. Terminate all processes unconditionally before returning.

findings.title: num_processes becomes 0 when no shards are assigned, silently disabling the flusher
findings.body: `self.max_processes = max_processes or len(buffer.assigned_shards)` plus `self.num_processes = min(self.max_processes, len(buffer.assigned_shards))` yields 0 when `buffer.assigned_shards` is empty (possible when a consumer is assigned no partitions). No flusher processes are started and no health check ever fires, so the strategy silently never flushes; additionally `max_processes` passed as 0 from the CLI would behave as "one process per shard" rather than an error. Validate the input and handle the empty-shard case explicitly.

findings.title: Dead method _create_process_for_shard
findings.body: `_create_process_for_shard(shard)` is not called from anywhere after the refactor (restarts go through `_create_process_for_shards`). Dead code that duplicates restart logic and will rot; remove it.

findings.title: Inconsistent metric tag name: 'shards' vs 'shard'
findings.body: `spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce` is tagged `shards=shard_tag` while `spans.buffer.flusher.produce` and `spans.buffer.segment_size_bytes` use `shard=shard_tag`. Inconsistent tag keys break dashboards/queries that group by one key. Pick one key name for all flusher metrics.

findings.title: Per-shard unhealthy metric increases cardinality and double-counts a single process failure
findings.body: `spans.buffer.flusher_unhealthy` is now emitted once per shard owned by the failing process, with a `shard` tag. One process failure produces N increments, so the metric no longer counts failures and the `shard` tag adds cardinality proportional to total shards. Consider emitting once per process (e.g. tagged with process index or the joined shard tag).

findings.title: New test asserts only process counts, not shard distribution or flushing correctness
findings.body: `test_flusher_processes_limit` checks `len(flusher.processes) == 2` and that the total shard count is 4, but never asserts that shards are evenly distributed (2 per process) nor that segments from all four shards actually get produced through the multiple processes. The core behaviour this PR introduces (parallel flushing across processes, restart handling) is untested.
